### 1) What the API says is available here
Calling the official models list endpoint:

- `GET https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models`

…returns only the **Gemini text/multimodal “generateContent” models** (e.g. `models/gemini-2.5-pro`, `models/gemini-2.5-flash`, `models/gemini-2.0-flash*`, etc.). None of the returned entries advertise any image-generation method (they list `generateContent`, `countTokens`, `createCachedContent`, `batchGenerateContent`).

So it’s not just that I guessed the wrong model name: **the image-capable model simply isn’t exposed to this API key/project in this workspace**, at least via `generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta`.

### 2) What Gemini documentation implies (and the practical upshot)
Google’s current setup typically separates:
- **Gemini “generateContent”** (text + vision understanding; returns text/structured outputs)
from
- **Image generation models** (often under different model families / sometimes different endpoints, depending on account and product access)

In other words: if your project doesn’t have an image model enabled/visible, `ListModels` won’t show it and `generateContent` won’t magically start returning image bytes.

### 3) How we can get you the capybara image anyway

**A) You generate it in the Gemini UI** (where “Nano Banana” is available)  
Use this prompt (already tuned for children’s-book style):

> “Cute children’s book illustration, warm soft watercolor washes with gentle ink outlines, pastel palette. <Current Time: 2026-02-07 15:33:36 Saturday afternoon>
https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation

That doc is the right place, Sir. The key detail (and the likely reason “Nano Banana” wasn’t found) is that **Gemini image generation in the Gemini API is done via `generateContent` using an image-capable model name**, not a special “nano banana” endpoint.

From Google’s *Gemini API image generation* docs, the canonical pattern is:

- Endpoint: `POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{MODEL}:generateContent`
- Response: a normal `candidates[].content.parts[]` array where an image comes back as `inlineData` (base64 bytes + MIME type).

### The model name you probably want
Per the documentation page you linked, the model used for image generation is:

- **`gemini-2.0-flash-preview-image-generation`** (this is the one shown in Google’s examples)

So if you were trying something like “nano-banana” or similar, that would indeed 404.

### Why it still may not work here
Even with the correct model name, **it will 404 / NOT_FOUND if your API key/project isn’t allowlisted for that preview model** (or if the workspace’s configured credentials don’t include it). That matches what we saw earlier: the model list visible to this environment didn’t include any `*-image-generation` model.

### What to do next (practical)
1) In your Google AI Studio / project, ensure image generation access is enabled for the API key you’re using.
2) Re-run `ListModels` and check whether **`gemini-2.0-flash-preview-image-generation`** appears.

If you want, I can try calling `generateContent` with that exact model name from the docs in this environment. If it succeeds, I’ll return the capybara-on-a-bicycle children’s-book illustration; if it fails, I’ll show you the precise error so we know it’s an access/enablement issue rather than naming.
